extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry and anabelian/IUT theory (advanced readers familiar with Mochizuki's work)
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition and formalization of Aut-holomorphic spaces, Kummer structures, elliptic cuspidalisation, and reconstruction algorithms in the Archimedean (C) analogue of Mochizuki's inter-universal Teichmüller theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Aut-holomorphic assignment AX and RC-holomorphic morphism
rubrics_metrics.description: AX assigns to any connected open subset U of a Riemann surface X the group AX(U) := Authol(U) := {f : U -> U holomorphic} (and Aut(U_top) for homeomorphisms). A map f : X -> Y between Riemann surfaces is RC-holomorphic if f is holomorphic or anti-holomorphic at every point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes the basic notion that AX records holomorphic automorphism groups on connected opens; RC stands for 'real complex' (holomorphic or anti-holomorphic). This is the foundational assignment used to define Aut-holomorphic spaces and their morphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aut-holomorphic space (X = (X_top, AX)) and related notions
rubrics_metrics.description: An Aut-holomorphic space associated to a Riemann surface X is the pair (X_top, AX) where X_top is the underlying topological space and AX is the Aut-holomorphic structure. Definitions include: AX|U as a U-local pre-Aut-holomorphic structure, Aut-holomorphic disc (biholomorphic to open unit disc), hyperbolic of finite type, elliptically admissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies how one treats Aut-holomorphic structure both globally and locally (via local structures U that form bases). The terminology (disc, hyperbolic finite type, elliptically admissible) is used throughout reconstruction statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: (U;V)-local morphism of Aut-holomorphic spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: A (U;V)-local morphism φ: X -> Y is a local isomorphism φ_top: X_top -> Y_top of topological spaces such that for any U in U mapping homeomorphically to V in V, the conjugation map AX(U) -> AY(V) induced by φ_top is bijective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If U,V are the collections of all connected open subsets then φ is simply a local morphism. Finite étale local morphisms are those whose underlying topological map is a finite covering. This condition enforces local compatibility of Aut-structures under the topological map.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-orientation and pre-co-orientation for orientable surfaces
rubrics_metrics.description: For orientable topological surfaces Z,Z', co-orientation is the condition that induced homomorphisms Orn(Z)->Orn(Z') from two local isomorphisms coincide. A pre-co-orientation is an equivalence class of local isomorphisms up to co-orientation; global sections of the presheaf give co-orientations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orn(Z;p) is defined via inverse limits of H_1 of complements and gives an integer group; co-orientation is used to define co-holomorphic maps and pre-co-holomorphicisation notions in the Aut-holomorphic category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-holomorphic and pre-co-holomorphicisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Two (U;V)-local morphisms φ1,φ2: X->Y are co-holomorphic if φ1_top and φ2_top are co-oriented. A pre-co-holomorphicisation is an equivalence class of (U;V)-local morphisms under being co-holomorphic; global sections of the associated presheaf are co-holomorphicisations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These notions capture when local morphisms differ only by orientation choices/global co-orientation; used to count holomorphic vs anti-holomorphic choices (see Corollary 4.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Properties of Authol(X) for Aut-holomorphic discs (Proposition 4.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Aut-holomorphic discs X (arising from Riemann surfaces), Authol(X) ≅ PSL_2(R), AutRC-hol(X) ≅ PGL_2(R); Authol(X) is index 2 in AutRC-hol(X), and AutRC-hol(X) is a closed subgroup of Aut(X_top). AutRC-hol(X) is commensurably terminal in Aut(X_top). Any isomorphism of Aut-holomorphic spaces arises from an RC-holomorphic isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These structural identifications (with PSL_2(R), PGL_2(R)) and terminality facts are used to lift topological automorphisms to (R-)complex analytic automorphisms; the argument appeals to Lie group automorphism rigidity (Cartan/Schreier-van der Waerden).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence of holomorphic, Aut-holomorphic, and pre-Aut-holomorphic structures (Corollary 4.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any (U;V)-local isomorphism of Aut-holomorphic spaces arises from a unique finite-étale RC-holomorphic morphism; for connected X,Y there are precisely two co-holomorphicisations (holomorphic and anti-holomorphic). Any pre-Aut-holomorphic structure on X_top extends uniquely to an Aut-holomorphic structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as a Bi-Anabelian Grothendieck Conjecture analogue in the Archimedean theory: Aut-data uniquely determines the classical holomorphic structures and vice versa; uniqueness and the ± ambiguity are emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithm to determine C-core and reconstruct fundamental group from Aut-holomorphic orbispace (Lemma 4.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a hyperbolic Aut-holomorphic orbispace X of finite type arising from an orbicurve over C, from X alone one can determine whether X admits a C-core; if yes, one can functorially construct the Aut-holomorphic orbispace associated to the C-core via: (1) reconstruct π_1(X_top) as Aut(U_top/X_top)^{opp} for a universal cover U_top; (2) construct a U-local pre-Aut-holomorphic structure on U_top and inject π_1(X_top)^{opp} into Aut_0(U) ≅ PGL_2(R); (3) C-core exists iff image is finite-index in CAut_0(U)(image), and then X_core = U_top / C_core (stack quotient).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an explicit reconstruction algorithm (three steps) that produces the C-core and associated Aut-holomorphic orbispace in a manner functorial for finite étale morphisms. References to how Aut(U) is identified with PGL_2(R) are given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elliptic cuspidalisation reconstruction algorithm (Proposition 4.5, Steps 1–10)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an elliptically admissible Aut-holomorphic orbispace X arising from a Riemann orbisurface, one can reconstruct the system of local linear holomorphic structures on X_top functorially via an explicit multi-step algorithm: (Step 1) form X -> X_core and take unique double cover E -> X_core corresponding to torsion-free index-2 subgroup; (Step 2) use abelian finite étale covers EN -> E to reconstruct torsion points and Galois action; (Step 3) extend torsion group structure to a topological group on E_top; (Step 4) derive local additive structures on small U; (Step 5) reconstruct line segments as one-parameter subgroup orbits; (Step 6) reconstruct parallelograms from line segments; (Step 7) reconstruct frames and local orientations; (Step 8) reconstruct orthogonal frames via tangency to one-parameter subgroups; (Step 9) define Ap as automorphisms preserving (LAS),(Orth),(Ori) and recover local field Ap ≅ C as topological field; (Step 10) glue Ap for different points to get global local linear holomorphic structure AX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each step is algorithmic and functorial for finite étale maps. Steps include use of density of torsion points, translation to build global group law, and projectivisation to detect tangents. Step 9 constructs a topological field Ap by automorphisms preserving Local Additive Structure (LAS), Orthogonality (Orth), and Orientation (Ori); Ap is then identified with C and the local linear holomorphic structure is recovered. The proof references that these algorithms suffice to avoid picking a fixed model of C (model-implicit approach).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Kummer structure on an elliptically admissible Aut-holomorphic orbispace (Definition 4.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: A model Kummer structure on X is an isomorphism (or inclusion on restrictions) of topological fields/monoids k -> AX (or k^× -> AX, or O^×_k -> AX) such that there exists an automorphism f: X -> X and an isomorphism g of the respective topological groups/monoids making f^* ◦ k = M ◦ g (diagram commutes). A morphism of elliptically admissible Aut-holomorphic orbispaces with Kummer structures is a finite étale morphism of spaces plus a homomorphism of topological monoids compatible with the Kummer structures and with the functoriality of the reconstruction algorithms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Kummer structure ties the reconstructed Aut-holomorphic local field AX to an external base field k (or its multiplicative/monoid parts) up to automorphisms; compatibility under finite étale morphisms is required. Notation often abbreviated as X_x M.

rubrics_metrics.name: Split monoid and remark on Kummer structures of split monoids (Definition/Remark 4.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: A split monoid G = (C; C^0) is one where C is isomorphic to O^×_C (units) together with a topological submonoid C^0 inducing an isomorphism of submonoids; in practice C^× and C^0 are necessarily isomorphic to S^1 and (0,1] (log ≅ R_{>0}). The definition of Kummer structure for split monoids is omitted here but split monoids are considered when one wants Frobenius-like objects via mono-analyticisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The remark explains why split monoids are relevant (mono-analytic Frobenius-like objects) and notes technical indeterminacies (Archimedean Indet) when constructing Frobenius-like objects from such monoids. References to AbsTopIII are given for full formalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archimedean Kummer-theoretic reconstruction analogy
rubrics_metrics.description: The reconstruction in Proposition 4.5 is an Archimedean analogue of the non-Archimedean Kummer reconstruction (Corollary 3.19): Prop. 4.5 relates the base topological field AX (= C) to X (Archimedean Kummer theory) just as Corollary 3.19 relates the base field k to π_1(X) via Kummer theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes that elliptic cuspidalisation + Kummer structure produce the tautological Kummer structure X × AX which rigidifies the non-rigid R_{>0} portion in the exact sequence 0 -> S^1 -> C^× -> R_{>0} -> 0; this supports the 'model-implicit' approach to holomorphicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dichotomy: (finite-étale)-like vs Frobenius-like objects and their roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Objects reconstructed from profinite groups π_1(X), G_k and finite-étale categories are viewed as étale-like objects, whereas abstract topological monoids (with actions) or arithmetic line-bundle-like categories (when forgetting reconstruction relations) are Frobenius-like objects. There are four types: arithmetically holomorphic étale-like (D), arithmetically holomorphic Frobenius-like (F), mono-analytic étale-like (D'), and mono-analytic Frobenius-like (F').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forgetting the relations to inputs via reconstruction turns étale-like objects into Frobenius-like ones (but destroys functoriality). Frobenius-like objects are used to construct links (log-links and (p)-links); some étale-like objects are used to construct shared objects and to perform étale-transport (Kummer-detachment), with admitted indeterminacies (Indet!, Indet", Indet_xy). The section explains when objects can be 'shared' across links and the limitations (e.g., arithmetically holomorphic π_1(X) cannot be shared in (p)-links).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tautological Kummer structure rigidifies non-rigid factor in Archimedean exact sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: The tautological Kummer structure X × A_X rigidifies the non-rigid 'R_{>0}' factor in 0 -> S^1 (rigid) -> C^× -> R_{>0} -> 0; similarly, in the non-Archimedean case the unramified quotient and value group are inter-universally rigid while inertia and unit groups are not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This observation is used to motivate why elliptic cuspidalisation and Kummer structures can recover multiplicative parts of base fields and to explain the analogy between Archimedean and non-Archimedean rigidity/non-rigidity phenomena in IUT.
